question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

The panel of experts ___ divided in their views on the proposed amendment.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. are.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A collective noun (panel, committee, jury, team, staff, audience) takes a singular verb when the group acts as one unit, and a plural verb when its members think or act individually. Here the experts are "divided in their views" — the plural pronoun "their" and the very idea of division show that individual opinions are meant, so the plural verb "are" is required.

◦ Complete sentence: The panel of experts are divided in their views on the proposed amendment.

 

• Consistency test: the verb and the pronoun that refers back to the noun must agree in number — The panel is unanimous in its view (one unit) but The panel are divided in their views (individual members).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "is" — the singular verb treats the panel as a single unit, which clashes with the plural pronoun "their" and with the meaning "divided".

 

• Option 3: "has been" — this is also a singular verb form, so it fails for the same reason as "is".

 

• Option 4: "was" — this is a singular past form, so it does not agree with the plural sense of the subject or with "their".

 

NOTE

 

• The jury has given its verdict (unit) but The jury are divided in their opinions (members). Other collective nouns: committee, board, staff, family, crew, audience, class, team, government.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Ten kilometres are (a)/ not a long distance (b)/ for an athlete (c)/ who trains daily. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When a plural noun of distance, time, money, weight or measure names a single total or unit, it takes a singular verb. "Ten kilometres" is one stretch of distance, so "is", not "are", is required. The singular complement "a long distance" also confirms this.

◦ Corrected sentence: Ten kilometres is not a long distance for an athlete who trains daily.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "not a long distance" is a proper singular complement, and it agrees with the singular verb "is".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "for an athlete" correctly uses "an" before the vowel sound of "athlete".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "who trains daily" is a proper relative clause, and "trains" agrees with the singular "athlete".

 

NOTE

 

• Fifty rupees is a fair price; Two hours is enough for the test; Ten kilos is too heavy for her. The plural verb is used only when the separate units are counted one by one.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

Hundred of protesters gathered outside the Collector's office demanding higher wages.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Hundreds of.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The words hundred, thousand, lakh, crore, million, dozen take "-s" and are followed by "of" when they show an indefinite, large number — hundreds of, thousands of, dozens of. With a definite number they stay singular and take no "of" (three hundred protesters). Here no exact number is given, so "Hundreds of" is needed.

◦ Corrected sentence: Hundreds of protesters gathered outside the Collector's office demanding higher wages.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "Hundred" — a bare "Hundred" cannot begin the sentence before a plural noun; even the definite form needs "a" or "one" (a hundred protesters), and it would then no longer express an indefinite number.

 

• Option 3: No substitution required — incorrect, because "Hundred of" mixes the singular numeral with "of", which is used only after the plural indefinite form.

 

• Option 4: "A hundreds of" — the article "a" cannot be used with the plural "hundreds".

 

NOTE

 

• two dozen eggs but dozens of eggs; five thousand rupees but thousands of rupees; three lakh votes but lakhs of votes.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The pair of scissors (a)/ that I bought yesterday (b)/ are already blunt. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Scissors, trousers, spectacles, pliers, tongs are plural-form nouns naming a single object made of two parts. Alone, they take a plural verb; but with the phrase "a pair of", the subject is the singular noun "pair", so the verb must be singular. "The pair of scissors … are" must be "is".

◦ Corrected sentence: The pair of scissors that I bought yesterday is already blunt.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The pair of scissors" is a proper subject whose head noun is "pair".

 

• Part (b) is correct — "that I bought yesterday" is a proper relative clause with the simple past.

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because the plural verb "are" in part (c) does not agree with "pair".

 

NOTE

 

• These scissors are sharp but This pair of scissors is sharp; My trousers are torn but My pair of trousers is torn. The same applies to a pair of spectacles / glasses / pliers / shoes.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

Academic merit is the only ___ for promotion in the department.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. criterion.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Criterion" is the singular and "criteria" the plural (the Greek pattern -on → -a). The words "the only" show that one standard is meant, so the singular "criterion" is required.

◦ Complete sentence: Academic merit is the only criterion for promotion in the department.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "criteria" — this is the plural form, and it cannot follow "the only" when a single standard is meant.

 

• Option 2: "criterias" — "criteria" is already plural, so adding "-s" gives a wrong double plural.

 

• Option 3: "criterions" — this is not the accepted plural in standard usage; the plural of "criterion" is "criteria".

 

NOTE

 

• -on → -a: criterion–criteria, phenomenon–phenomena. -um → -a: bacterium–bacteria, medium–media, curriculum–curricula. -us → -i: alumnus–alumni, stimulus–stimuli, radius–radii. -is → -es: hypothesis–hypotheses, thesis–theses.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Many a (a)/ promising cricketer (b)/ have been ruined (c)/ by lack of proper guidance. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Many a" is always followed by a singular noun and a singular verb, even though the meaning is plural. So "have been ruined" must be "has been ruined".

◦ Corrected sentence: Many a promising cricketer has been ruined by lack of proper guidance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Many a" is the proper determiner before a singular noun.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "promising cricketer" is a proper singular noun phrase after "Many a".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "by lack of proper guidance" is a proper prepositional phrase showing the agent or cause.

 

NOTE

 

• Many a student has failed means Many students have failed. In the same way, more than one + singular noun takes a singular verb: More than one candidate has withdrawn.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

The consumer court ordered the builder to pay ₹5 lakh as damage to the flat owners for the delay in possession.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. as damages.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Some nouns change their meaning between the singular and the plural. "Damage" (uncountable) means harm or injury, but "damages" (always plural) means money paid as compensation by order of a court. As the builder is ordered to pay ₹5 lakh, the required word is "damages".

◦ Corrected sentence: The consumer court ordered the builder to pay ₹5 lakh as damages to the flat owners for the delay in possession.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "as damage's" — the possessive form has no meaning here, and the apostrophe is not needed.

 

• Option 2: "as a damage" — "damage" in the sense of harm is uncountable and cannot take "a"; it also does not mean compensation.

 

• Option 4: No substitution required — incorrect, because the singular "damage" does not carry the meaning of monetary compensation.

 

NOTE

 

• Meaning changes: custom (habit) – customs (duty at the border); manner (way) – manners (etiquette); air (atmosphere) – airs (pretentious behaviour); pain (suffering) – pains (effort); regard (respect) – regards (greetings).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The airline has ordered (a)/ twelve new aircrafts (b)/ to expand its fleet (c)/ on international routes. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Aircraft" has the same form in the singular and the plural; it never takes "-s". So "twelve new aircrafts" must be "twelve new aircraft".

◦ Corrected sentence: The airline has ordered twelve new aircraft to expand its fleet on international routes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The airline has ordered" is a proper present perfect verb phrase with a singular subject.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "to expand its fleet" is a proper infinitive of purpose, and "its" agrees with the singular "airline".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "on international routes" is a proper prepositional phrase.

 

NOTE

 

• Same form in both numbers: aircraft, spacecraft, hovercraft, series, species, sheep, deer, salmon, offspring. But crafts is correct when the word means skills or handicrafts (arts and crafts).

question: Select the sentence that is grammatically correct.
option_1: The teacher gave us some useful advice on how to prepare for the interview.
option_2: The committee has gathered enough evidences to file a chargesheet.
option_3: Rahul has made a remarkable progress in his studies this year.
option_4: The workshop was well stocked with modern equipments.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The teacher gave us some useful advice on how to prepare for the interview.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Only Option 1 is correct. "Advice" is an uncountable noun: it takes "some" and never a plural "-s" or the article "a".

◦ Correct sentence: The teacher gave us some useful advice on how to prepare for the interview.

 

• Each of the other three options wrongly treats an uncountable noun as countable, as explained below.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "enough evidences" — "evidence" is uncountable and has no plural; the correct form is "enough evidence" (or "enough pieces of evidence").

 

• Option 3: "a remarkable progress" — "progress" is uncountable and cannot take "a"; the correct form is "remarkable progress".

 

• Option 4: "modern equipments" — "equipment" is uncountable and has no plural; the correct form is "modern equipment".

 

NOTE

 

• Uncountable nouns: advice, evidence, progress, equipment, information, furniture, luggage, knowledge, homework, news. To count them, use a partner phrase — a piece of advice, an item of equipment, two pieces of evidence.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

A rainbow is a natural phenomena (a)/ caused by the refraction (b)/ of sunlight (c)/ in water droplets. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Phenomena" is the plural of "phenomenon" (Greek -on → -a). After the singular article "a" and the singular verb "is", the singular "phenomenon" is needed.

◦ Corrected sentence: A rainbow is a natural phenomenon caused by the refraction of sunlight in water droplets.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "caused by the refraction" is a proper past participle phrase modifying "phenomenon".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "of sunlight" is a proper prepositional phrase showing what is refracted.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "in water droplets" is a proper prepositional phrase, and "water" acts as a noun modifier.

 

NOTE

 

• Foreign plurals used as singulars is a common trap — a criteria ✗ (a criterion), a bacteria ✗ (a bacterium), an alumni ✗ (an alumnus), a media ✗ (a medium).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

The ___ of the disease was delayed because the local laboratory lacked proper equipment.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. diagnosis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• After the article "The" and before "of", a noun is required. The noun is "diagnosis" (singular), and the singular verb "was delayed" confirms that a singular noun is needed.

◦ Complete sentence: The diagnosis of the disease was delayed because the local laboratory lacked proper equipment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "diagnose" — this is a verb and cannot follow "The" as the subject of "was delayed".

 

• Option 2: "diagnoses" — this is the plural of "diagnosis" (or a verb form); a plural subject would need "were delayed", not "was delayed".

 

• Option 3: "diagnosed" — this is a past verb or participle, not a noun, so it cannot fill the subject position.

 

NOTE

 

• Nouns ending in -is form the plural with -es: diagnosis–diagnoses, crisis–crises, analysis–analyses, basis–bases, oasis–oases. Verb–noun pairs: diagnose–diagnosis, analyse–analysis.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

The customer care centre received a large amount of complaints after the sudden hike in electricity tariff.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. a large number of complaints.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Number" is used with countable plural nouns, while "amount" is used with uncountable nouns (an amount of money / water / time). "Complaints" is a countable plural noun, so the correct expression is "a large number of complaints".

◦ Corrected sentence: The customer care centre received a large number of complaints after the sudden hike in electricity tariff.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: No substitution required — incorrect, because "amount" cannot be used with a countable plural noun like "complaints".

 

• Option 2: "a great deal of complaints" — "a great deal of" is used only with uncountable nouns (a great deal of trouble).

 

• Option 4: "a large amount of complaint" — the singular "complaint" is countable and cannot take "amount"; the meaning also becomes unnatural.

 

NOTE

 

• a number of students but an amount of money; many / few / fewer + countable but much / little / less + uncountable; a large quantity of can be used with both types.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Statistics are (a)/ a difficult subject (b)/ for many students (c)/ of commerce. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The names of branches of study ending in "-ics" — statistics, mathematics, physics, economics, politics, ethics — are treated as singular and take a singular verb. Here "Statistics" means the subject, and the complement "a difficult subject" is singular, so "is" is required.

◦ Corrected sentence: Statistics is a difficult subject for many students of commerce.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "a difficult subject" is a proper singular noun phrase that agrees with the verb "is".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "for many students" is a proper prepositional phrase, and "students" is a correct plural.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "of commerce" is a proper prepositional phrase showing the field of study.

 

NOTE

 

• The plural verb is used when the word means numerical data or personal qualities: The latest statistics are alarming; His politics are questionable. But for the subject: Physics is interesting, Economics is a social science.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The brave soldiers laid down (a)/ their life for the country (b)/ during the war. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The distributive plural rule: when a plural subject refers to things that each person has one of (life, hand, head), the noun must also be plural. Many soldiers each laid down a life, so "their lives" is correct, not "their life".

◦ Corrected sentence: The brave soldiers laid down their lives for the country during the war.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The brave soldiers laid down" is a proper plural subject with the simple past of "lay down".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "during the war" is a proper prepositional phrase of time.

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "their life" in part (b) is incorrect.

 

NOTE

 

• The students raised their hands; The judges shook their heads; All the workers risked their lives; The guests took off their hats — each person owns one, but the noun still stays plural.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

The High Court has banned the practise of employing children in hazardous factories.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. practice of.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In British spelling, the noun is spelt "practice" (with c) and the verb "practise" (with s). After "the", a noun is needed, and the noun takes the preposition "of" before the gerund: "the practice of employing".

◦ Corrected sentence: The High Court has banned the practice of employing children in hazardous factories.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "practice for" — the noun spelling is right, but "practice" takes "of" before a gerund, not "for".

 

• Option 2: "practises of" — "practises" is the verb form (third person singular) and cannot follow "the".

 

• Option 4: No substitution required — incorrect, because "practise" is the verb spelling and cannot be used as a noun.

 

NOTE

 

• Noun–verb spelling pairs (British): practice–practise, licence–license, advice–advise, prophecy–prophesy, device–devise. The noun ends in -ce and the verb in -se; a simple test is to compare advice / advise in pronunciation.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

Before his death, the old landlord divided his estate equally among his three ___.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. sons-in-law.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a compound noun made of a noun + a prepositional phrase, the plural "-s" is added to the main noun — the first word — and not to the end. The main noun here is "son", so the plural is "sons-in-law".

◦ Complete sentence: Before his death, the old landlord divided his estate equally among his three sons-in-law.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "son-in-laws" — the "-s" has been added to the last word, but the head noun is "son".

 

• Option 2: "sons-in-laws" — this puts the plural on both parts; only the head noun takes "-s".

 

• Option 3: "son's-in-law" — this is a possessive-like form, and "son" stays singular, so it does not fit "three ___".

 

NOTE

 

• mothers-in-law, brothers-in-law, commanders-in-chief, courts-martial, lookers-on, hangers-on, runners-up. The possessive goes on the last word: my brother-in-law's car.

question: Select the sentence in which the underlined noun is used incorrectly.
option_1: The counsel for the accused urged the court to grant bail.
option_2: The government has identified a suitable sight for the proposed airport.
option_3: The Municipal Council has approved the plan for a new flyover.
option_4: The board has recruited fresh personnel for the accounts department.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The government has identified a suitable sight for the proposed airport.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Option 2, "sight" (the ability to see, or something seen) is the wrong noun. A place chosen to build something is a "site", so the sentence should read "a suitable site for the proposed airport".

◦ Corrected sentence: The government has identified a suitable site for the proposed airport.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 is correct — "counsel" means a lawyer or legal adviser, so "the counsel for the accused" is properly used.

 

• Option 3 is correct — "council" means an elected or advisory body, so "the Municipal Council" is properly used.

 

• Option 4 is correct — "personnel" means the staff of an organisation, so "fresh personnel for the accounts department" is properly used.

 

NOTE

 

• Confusable nouns: site (place) / sight (vision) / cite (verb: to quote); council (body) / counsel (advice, lawyer); personnel (staff) / personal (adjective: private); principal / principle; stationary / stationery.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Electric vehicles are becoming popular (a)/ among urban commuters (b)/ because of rising fuel prices, (c)/ and there is a growing demand of them. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Certain nouns take a fixed preposition. The noun "demand" is followed by "for" (demand for), not "of". So "a growing demand of them" must be "a growing demand for them".

◦ Corrected sentence: Electric vehicles are becoming popular among urban commuters because of rising fuel prices, and there is a growing demand for them.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Electric vehicles are becoming popular" is a proper present continuous with a plural subject.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "among urban commuters" is a proper prepositional phrase, and "among" suits a group of three or more.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "because of rising fuel prices," is a proper prepositional phrase giving the reason.

 

NOTE

 

• Noun + preposition: demand for, need for, respect for, reason for, cause of, solution to, answer to, reply to, access to, interest in, objection to, prejudice against, influence on.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

The district hospital has recently appointed four ___ to improve healthcare for expectant mothers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. women doctors.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When a compound noun begins with "man" or "woman" as a modifier before another noun, both words take the plural — men servants, women doctors, gentlemen farmers. With "four", both the modifier and the noun must be plural: "women doctors".

◦ Complete sentence: The district hospital has recently appointed four women doctors to improve healthcare for expectant mothers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "woman doctors" — the modifier stays singular, but in this pattern both words must be plural.

 

• Option 3: "women doctor" — only the modifier is plural, and the noun after the numeral "four" must also be plural.

 

• Option 4: "womens doctors" — "women" is already an irregular plural and does not take "-s"; the form "womens" does not exist.

 

NOTE

 

• men employees, women workers, gentlemen officers. Do not confuse this with a man-servant / a woman doctor (singular), where both words are singular.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The company has (a)/ employed a team to look after (b)/ the maintainance (c)/ of its machines. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The noun form of the verb "maintain" is "maintenance" (main-ten-ance). The spelling "maintainance" is wrong, because the noun does not keep the "-tain" of the verb.

◦ Corrected sentence: The company has employed a team to look after the maintenance of its machines.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The company has" is a proper singular subject with the correct auxiliary.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "employed a team to look after" is a proper verb phrase, with "look after" meaning to take care of.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "of its machines" is a proper prepositional phrase, and "its" agrees with the singular "company".

 

NOTE

 

• Spelling of noun forms: pronounce–pronunciation (not pronounciation), maintain–maintenance, occur–occurrence, convenient–convenience, acquaint–acquaintance, argue–argument.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The chiefs of the two departments (a)/ inspected the roofs of the buildings (b)/ damaged by the storm. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sentence is grammatically correct. Nouns ending in -f such as chief, roof, proof, belief, cliff, safe form the plural by simply adding "-s" — chiefs, roofs. They do not change to "-ves".

◦ Sentence as given: The chiefs of the two departments inspected the roofs of the buildings damaged by the storm.

 

• The past participle phrase "damaged by the storm" correctly modifies "the buildings".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "chiefs" is the proper plural of "chief", and "of the two departments" is a proper phrase.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "inspected the roofs of the buildings" is a proper verb phrase, and "roofs" is the proper plural of "roof".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "damaged by the storm" is a proper past participle phrase in the passive sense.

 

NOTE

 

• -f / -fe → -ves: leaf–leaves, wolf–wolves, half–halves, wife–wives, knife–knives, thief–thieves. -f → -s only: chief–chiefs, roof–roofs, proof–proofs, belief–beliefs, cliff–cliffs, safe–safes.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

The mountain resort offers a breathtaking scenery that attracts thousands of tourists every winter.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. breathtaking scenery.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Scenery" is an uncountable noun. It cannot take the article "a" and has no plural form. The correct phrase is "breathtaking scenery", and the singular verb "attracts" agrees with it.

◦ Corrected sentence: The mountain resort offers breathtaking scenery that attracts thousands of tourists every winter.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "the breathtaking sceneries" — "sceneries" does not exist as a plural, and it would not agree with the singular verb "attracts".

 

• Option 3: No substitution required — incorrect, because the article "a" cannot be used with the uncountable noun "scenery".

 

• Option 4: "breathtaking sceneries" — "scenery" has no plural form.

 

NOTE

 

• Use a view / a landscape / a sight for a countable sense. Uncountable: scenery, luggage, baggage, machinery, furniture, jewellery, mail, weather, traffic.

question: Select the sentence in which the possessive form is used correctly.
option_1: The Prime Minister's of India speech was telecast live.
option_2: The hotel is only a stone throw away from the railway station.
option_3: She is a close friend of my father's.
option_4: Mens' and womens' shoes are sold on the ground floor.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. She is a close friend of my father's.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Only Option 3 is correct. It uses the double possessive (a / this / that + noun + of + possessive): "a close friend of my father's". The 's after "father" is required here, because the idea is "one of my father's friends".

◦ Correct sentence: She is a close friend of my father's.

 

• Each of the other three options contains a different possessive error, explained below.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "The Prime Minister's of India speech" — in a group genitive, the 's is added to the last word of the whole phrase: "The Prime Minister of India's speech".

 

• Option 2: "a stone throw" — the fixed idiom is "a stone's throw", with the possessive 's.

 

• Option 4: "Mens' and womens'" — "men" and "women" are irregular plurals not ending in "s", so they take 's: "Men's and women's shoes".

 

NOTE

 

• a friend of mine / of his / of Ravi's; this habit of my brother's. Irregular plurals: children's, men's, women's, people's; regular plurals: girls', teachers', engineers'.

question: Select the sentence in which the plural form of the noun is used incorrectly.
option_1: The museum has preserved the formulae written by the great mathematician.
option_2: The stimuli used in the experiment were carefully chosen.
option_3: The hunters set traps to catch the wolves roaming near the village.
option_4: The scientist tested three different hypothesis before publishing the results.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The scientist tested three different hypothesis before publishing the results.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Option 4, "three different hypothesis" is wrong, because the numeral "three" needs a plural noun. Nouns ending in -is form the plural with -es, so it must be "hypotheses".

◦ Corrected sentence: The scientist tested three different hypotheses before publishing the results.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 is correct — "formulae" is a proper Latin plural of "formula" (the plural "formulas" is also accepted).

 

• Option 2 is correct — "stimuli" is the proper plural of "stimulus" (-us → -i), and the plural verb "were" agrees with it.

 

• Option 3 is correct — "wolves" is the proper plural of "wolf" (f → ves).

 

NOTE

 

• hypothesis–hypotheses, thesis–theses, parenthesis–parentheses, axis–axes. Also remember stimulus–stimuli, radius–radii, syllabus–syllabi (or syllabuses), focus–foci.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

To curb the menace of cyber fraud, Parliament has enacted a stringent new ___ that prescribes imprisonment for offenders.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. statute.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A "statute" is a written law passed by a legislature. As Parliament has enacted a law that prescribes imprisonment, the required noun is "statute".

◦ Complete sentence: To curb the menace of cyber fraud, Parliament has enacted a stringent new statute that prescribes imprisonment for offenders.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "statue" — a statue is a carved or cast figure of a person or animal, and it cannot be "enacted".

 

• Option 3: "stature" — this means a person's height or standing, and it is not something that Parliament enacts.

 

• Option 4: "status" — this means a person's position or legal condition, and it does not prescribe imprisonment.

 

NOTE

 

• A similar-sounding trio: statue (figure) / stature (height, reputation) / statute (law). Also note status (position) and statutory (adjective, required by law).
